description: The same 240px card as card-default, with a long heading and a multi-sentence paragraph — both children must wrap across several lines and the card must grow to fit them.

florui.css: .card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 240px; padding-top: 16px; padding-right: 16px; padding-bottom: 16px; padding-left: 16px; border-top-width: 1px; border-top-style: solid; border-top-color: #d0d0d0; border-right-width: 1px; border-right-style: solid; border-right-color: #d0d0d0; border-bottom-width: 1px; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-color: #d0d0d0; border-left-width: 1px; border-left-style: solid; border-left-color: #d0d0d0; background-color: #fafafa; } .card h2 { margin-top: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-bottom: 8px; margin-left: 0px; } .card p { margin-top: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; }

children.text: A longer card title that itself wraps

This paragraph is deliberately long content, spanning several sentences so it wraps across multiple lines inside the same fixed-width card that the default fixture also uses. It exists to prove the card grows to fit real content rather than clipping or overflowing it.

classification.reason: Measured live against Chromium: 12.44% pixel diff, 3.0px max geometry delta (both real numbers, not guesses). Both higher than the bare-element fixtures' own calibration because this content wraps across roughly 8 lines instead of 1-2 — the anaglyph overlay (florui_vs_chromium.png from a real `florui compare` run) shows every line of text fully legible and correctly positioned, with a thin, gradually-growing antialiasing fringe toward the bottom: tiny per-line float rounding in text shaping/line-height math accumulating across more lines, the same already-documented source as the bare-element fixtures' own small deltas, not a wrap-point or layout divergence.
